title: K-injective replacement is an exact functor to the homotopy category
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with a chosen unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and assume that every cochain complex has a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex. Here $I$ is K-injective if every chain map from an acyclic complex to $I$ is null-homotopic. Write $K(\mathcal A)$ for cochain complexes modulo homotopy, with its usual cone triangulation, and $K_{\mathrm{inj}}(\mathcal A)$ for its full subcategory on K-injectives. This subcategory is closed under shifts and cones, and localization restricts to a triangulated equivalence $q:K_{\mathrm{inj}}(\mathcal A)\simeq D(\mathcal A)$. In particular, for any chosen quasi-inverse $q^{-1}$, the functor $R=\iota\circ q^{-1}:D(\mathcal A)\to K(\mathcal A)$, where $\iota$ is the inclusion, admits coherent commutation with all integer shifts and is triangulated [def-weil-triangulated-category]; its opposite $R^{\mathrm{op}}:D(\mathcal A)^{\mathrm{op}}\to K(\mathcal A)^{\mathrm{op}}$ is triangulated with the opposite shift structures. These assertions apply in particular to the chosen inverse of upstream `HomotopyCategory.KInjectives.Qh` used in `DerivedCategory.bifunctorRHomOfComplex`. No exactness property of an internal-Hom bifunctor is asserted.

proof.text: By [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated], $K(\mathcal A)$ has the cone triangulation and $Q:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ is exact. Let $\mathcal P$ be its acyclic objects. The shift of an acyclic complex is acyclic, since $H^r(M[n])=H^{r+n}(M)=0$. The stated definition of K-injectivity identifies $K_{\mathrm{inj}}(\mathcal A)$ with $\mathcal P^\perp$: a homotopy class is zero precisely when a representative is null-homotopic. Apply [lem-sf-shift-stable-right-orthogonal] to obtain repleteness, zero, shifts and two-of-three, in particular closure under cones. By [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory] it inherits the triangulation and its inclusion $\iota$ is exact.

For K-injectives $I,J$, [lem-sc-kinjective-quasi-iso-comparison] gives bijectivity of $\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(I,J)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D}(QI,QJ)$. Since the K-injective subcategory is full, this is exactly the map on morphisms for $q=Q\iota$. Thus $q$ is fully faithful. By [lem-trf-localization-essentially-surjective] every derived object is isomorphic to $Q(M)$ for some complex $M$. Choose a quasi-isomorphism $M\to I$ with $I$ K-injective using the hypothesis. Localization inverts it, so $Q(M)\cong Q(I)=q(I)$. Therefore $q$ is essentially surjective, and [lem-trf-fully-faithful-ess-surj-equivalence] makes it an equivalence.

The shift comparison of $q=Q\iota$ is the composite of those of $Q$ and $\iota$. Their zero and addition coherence equations compose; a distinguished triangle is first sent by $\iota$ to a distinguished triangle of $K(\mathcal A)$ and then by $Q$ to one of $D(\mathcal A)$. Thus $q$ is exact. For any chosen quasi-inverse $G$, choose the equivalence unit and counit. Equip $G$ with the comparisons uniquely determined by requiring its counit $qG\cong\mathrm{id}$ to commute with shifts: the comparison $G(X[n])\to(GX)[n]$ is the unique lift under fully faithful $q$ of the isomorphism $qG(X[n])\cong X[n]\cong(qGX)[n]\cong q((GX)[n])$. Naturality and zero/addition coherence follow after applying faithful $q$, where they are the corresponding equations for $q$ and the counit. The equivalence triangle identities give the unit compatibility. Apply [lem-trf-exact-equivalence-inverse] to conclude that $G$ is exact. Finally $R=\iota G$ has the composite coherent shift comparison and takes triangles successively to distinguished triangles under $G$ and $\iota$.

Apply [lem-sf-triangulated-functor-opposite] to the exact functor $R$. Its hypotheses hold by step 3, so $R^{\mathrm{op}}$ has coherent shifts and preserves distinguished triangles for the opposite shift and triangle conventions, giving the asserted opposite exactness.

In the upstream model, HomotopyCategory.KInjectives is the full right orthogonal of acyclics and its Qh is the inclusion followed by DerivedCategory.Qh. Consequently its chosen inverse is a particular $G$ in step 3; the construction does not require any particular choice. The definition of DerivedCategory.bifunctorRHomOfComplex uses exactly this inverse followed by that inclusion before applying the Hom-complex functor and leftOp. Thus steps 3 and 4 apply to its replacement factor and its opposite.

lean.statement: theorem replacement_triangulated (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} C] (h : ∀ K : CochainComplex C ℤ, ∃ (I : CochainComplex C ℤ) (i : K ⟶ I), I.IsKInjective ∧ QuasiIso i) : (subcategoryAcyclic C).rightOrthogonal.IsTriangulated ∧ CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated (KInjectives C) ∧ (ι (C := C)).IsTriangulated ∧ (Qh (C := C)).IsEquivalence ∧ (Qh (C := C)).IsTriangulated ∧ ∀ (G : DerivedCategory C ⥤ KInjectives C) (η : 𝟭 (KInjectives C) ≅ Qh ⋙ G) (ε : G ⋙ Qh ≅ 𝟭 (DerivedCategory C)), ∃ S : G.CommShift ℤ, (fun [s : G.CommShift ℤ] ↦ G.IsTriangulated ∧ (G ⋙ ι).IsTriangulated ∧ (G ⋙ ι).op.IsTriangulated) (s := S)
lean.note: Uses the existing upstream full subcategory and Qh, with their inherited/composite CommShift structures supplied as real instance data. The resolution hypothesis requires only a quasi-isomorphism, not a monomorphism. The universal quasi-inverse clause covers the chosen Qh.inv used by bifunctorRHomOfComplex.
